newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade surplus slips, c/a deficit narrows.
newsitem.headline: German trade surplus slips, c/a deficit narrows.

text.p: Germany's trade surplus slipped back in August from July but was still up on a year earlier, while the current account deficit narrowed, the Federal Statistics Office said on Friday.
Preliminary data showed that the surplus fell to 8.1 billion marks in August from 10.3 billion marks in July, but was still up on 6.9 billion marks from a year earlier.
Meanwhile, the current account was 4.6 billion marks in the red, narrowing from five billion marks in July and 5.3 billion marks in August 1995.

Exports in August were 58.3 billion marks, down on July's 69.1 billion marks, but still up on 56.9 billion marks a year earlier. Meanwhile imports were 50.3 billion marks, down from 58.8 billion in July and little changed on year-ago levels.
